title: SAML session heuristics: JIT provisioning edge cases, MFA step-up expectations, logout coordination
creator: Daniel Kim
description:
Background: As we onboard more enterprise customers using SAML/SSO, we have inconsistent behavior across session lifecycle events: JIT-provisioned users sometimes lack expected RBAC roles until a background sync, MFA expectations are unclear for step-up flows, Single-Logout (SLO) propagation is flaky across our hosted and dedicated runtimes, and audit logs miss key SSO lifecycle events. This ticket defines heuristics and engineering changes to make SSO sessions deterministic, auditable, and administratively controllable.

Problem statement: Customers expect: 1) immediate and predictable RBAC role assignment for JIT-created users, 2) consistent MFA step-up or re-auth behavior for sensitive actions, 3) reliable logout propagation (IdP-initiated and SP-initiated), and 4) complete audit trails for SSO events (JIT create, role assignment, MFA challenge/outcome, logout). Current gaps cause operational confusion and security risk during compliance reviews.
acceptance_criteria: 1) JIT-provisioning flow assigns initial role mapping deterministically from attribute mapping or default role and emits an SSO_JIT_CREATE_USER audit event. 2) If RBAC v2 role mapping fails or is delayed, user receives a clear ephemeral 'provisioning_pending' session flag and limited privileges until resolution. 3) MFA step-up is triggered for configurable sensitive actions (token_create, api_key_rotate, admin_console), with clear event sequence MFA_CHALLENGE -> MFA_PASS/MFA_FAIL in audit logs. 4) IdP-initiated SLO and SP-initiated logout both mark sessions as revoked in backend session store and emit SSO_LOGOUT_INITIATED and SSO_SLO_SUCCESS/SSO_SP_LOGOUT events. 5) Admin console has a 'force sign-out' control that invalidates active sessions for a user or entire org with an admin audit event. 6) No regression in latency >1% on token issuance paths in hosted API during rollout (measured using canary).
technical_design:
Overview: Implement a small session state machine in the session store (session_state: active | provisioning_pending | revoked | reauth_required) with transitions driven by SAML assertions and platform events. Key changes: 

- JIT provisioning: On first successful SAML assertion, create user record and attempt immediate role mapping via RBAC v2 sync path. If mapping succeeds, transition session->active and attach roles. If mapping fails (attribute missing or external role fetch timeout), create session with session_state=provisioning_pending and apply minimal 'guest-provision' policy. Emit audit event SSO_JIT_CREATE_USER with fields (saml_issuer, nameid, attributes_snapshot, role_map_status).

- RBAC v2 integration: Introduce an atomic 'role_assignment_id' with status values (assigned | pending | failed) surfaced in audit logs. Add short-term background job to reconcile pending mappings; reconcile attempts backoff exponentially up to 5 minutes. If still pending after grace period, notify org admins via console notification and email (configurable).

- MFA step-up: Define a configurable policy list of sensitive actions. On attempt, check last_authn_time and mfa_verified_at; if beyond threshold or mfa not present, set session_state=reauth_required and respond with 401 + WWW-Authenticate header 'x-redwood-stepup: mfa'. Record audit events MFA_CHALLENGE and outcome (MFA_PASS/MFA_FAIL) with correlation_id linking to original SAML session ID.

- Logout and SLO: Support both front-channel SLO and back-channel SAML logout. For IdP-initiated SLO, validate LogoutRequest signature, mark all sessions for the NameID as revoked, and emit SSO_LOGOUT_INITIATED and SSO_SLO_SUCCESS. For SP-initiated logout, send LogoutRequest to IdP if configured, but immediately mark local session revoked for UX. Add robust retry for SLO delivery failures and surface delivery status in audit logs.

- Session refresh and grace windows: Token refresh allowed when session_state=active and last_authn_time within refresh_window (default 24h). If outside refresh_window, set session_state=reauth_required and reject refresh. Reauth grace period configurable per org (default 10 minutes) to allow interactive reauth without losing state for short interruptions.

- Audit logging: Add structured audit events for: SSO_LOGIN, SSO_JIT_CREATE_USER, ROLE_ASSIGNMENT_{ASSIGNED|PENDING|FAILED}, MFA_CHALLENGE, MFA_PASS, MFA_FAIL, SSO_LOGOUT_INITIATED, SSO_SLO_SUCCESS, SSO_SP_LOGOUT, TOKEN_REFRESH, SESSION_REVOKED, REAUTH_REQUIRED. Each event must include timestamp, subject_id, nameid, saml_issuer, session_id, actor (system|idp|user|admin), and correlation_id. Logs should be emitted to our audit pipeline (Kafka topic audit-sso) with schema v2.

- Admin controls: Expose API endpoints: POST /admin/orgs/{org}/sessions/invalidate and POST /admin/users/{user}/sessions/invalidate which accept filters (all, device_id, issue_before). These calls create admin audit events ADMIN_FORCE_SIGNOUT and trigger immediate revoke transitions. Console UX to list active sessions with session_state and revoke button.

- Backwards compatibility: Keep existing tokens valid until revoked to avoid mass logout during rollout. The session_state tape will be consulted for new checks; legacy tokens without session_state map to active but will be migrated on next renewal or sign-in.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind org-level flag 'saml_session_v2'. 2) Implement audit producers and small state machine in session store service (session-service). 3) Canary to 5% orgs for 48 hours, monitor error rates and latency. 4) Enable JIT deterministic role mapping for canary orgs only; keep background reconciliation enabled. 5) After 72h and no critical issues, expand to 50% then 100% over 7 days. 6) Enable admin console controls last after audit trails validated. 7) Communicate breaking changes: none expected; document new admin APIs and default reauth windows in release notes.
testing_and_validation:
Unit tests: session state transitions, role_assignment backoff and reconciliation, MFA challenge flow, logout propagation handlers. Integration tests: full SAML flow with IdP simulator covering: normal sign-in, JIT create + immediate role mapping, JIT create + mapping failure, IdP-initiated SLO, SP-initiated logout, MFA step-up. Load tests: ensure token issuance path latency increase <1% under normal load; simulate 10k concurrent SAML logins to validate session-store scaling. Security tests: pen-test of logout endpoints, signature validation, replay protection. Acceptance QA checklist included below.

QA checklist: 
- [ ] SSO_JIT_CREATE_USER event appears in audit stream for JIT users.
- [ ] Role assignation success and failure events logged.
- [ ] MFA step-up produces challenge and correct audit outcome.
- [ ] IdP SLO revokes sessions across multiple devices.
- [ ] Admin force sign-out invalidates active tokens and emits ADMIN_FORCE_SIGNOUT event.
- [ ] Reauth grace window honored across browser refresh and mobile clients.
monitoring_and_audit_requirements:
Create dashboards: 1) SAML sign-in rate, JIT success rate, JIT failure reasons. 2) Role assignment pending count and time-to-resolve. 3) MFA challenge rate and failure rate. 4) SLO success/failure ratio and retry counts. 5) Admin force signout counts. Instrument metrics: sso.jit.create.total, sso.jit.create.failed, sso.role.assignment.latency_ms, sso.mfa.challenge.total, sso.mfa.fail.rate, sso.logout.slo.success, audit.events.emitted. Alerts: JIT failure rate >2% for 30m, role assignment backlog >1000, SLO failure rate >5% for 15m, audit pipeline lag >60s. Ensure Kafka topic retention and consumer groups configured for audit-sso.

Event schema documentation should be published in internal Confluence with example JSON payloads and mapping to external SIEM fields for enterprise customers.
